author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New York City has released more than 170,000 pages of records documenting its response to the September 11 attacks and the years that followed, including files tied to health and air-quality concerns.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the disclosure Tuesday, September 8. Reuters reported that the release accompanies settlements in two lawsuits seeking access to post-9/11 records. The city’s action makes a large body of material available ahead of the attacks’ 25th anniversary.

The records could help survivors, families, researchers and journalists trace what officials knew, how agencies communicated and how environmental and health concerns were handled. Their volume also means meaningful review will take time; releasing pages does not by itself establish what individual documents show.

Questions about exposure and long-term illness have remained central to the public record of the disaster and cleanup. The disclosure creates an opportunity for independent examination, but conclusions should be tied to specific documents and supporting evidence. Additional reporting may identify gaps, duplicated material or records that require context from the agencies that created them.
dek: The disclosure documents the city’s response to the attacks and aftermath and resolves two lawsuits seeking access to health and air-quality files.
headline: New York City releases 170,000 pages of post-9/11 health and air records
